findings.title: rawTokenId null-check inspects grantType instead
findings.body: AccessTokenContext's constructor calls Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") instead of checking rawTokenId. A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted (the message is also wrong). encodeTokenId then concatenates that null into the jti, producing a token id whose raw id is the literal string "null", and later lookups or revocation keyed by the real generated id will miss the token.

findings.title: Access-token id matcher rejects matches and checks the wrong slice
findings.body: isAccessTokenId is inverted and off by one. Encoded ids are ssttgg:uuid (grant shortcut at indexes 4-5), but the matcher uses items[0].substring(3, 5) and returns false when that slice equals the expected shortcut. For a normal regular token the slice is the last token-type character plus the first grant character (e.g. "ta" for onrtac), which never equals "ac"/"rt"/"dg"/"ci", so the equality check never fires and the matcher only verifies that something after ':' looks like a UUID. expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken, and expectAuthReqIdToToken therefore stay green even if the grant shortcut is missing or wrong, and a token whose chars 3-4 happen to equal the expected shortcut is failed.

findings.title: Grant shortcut contract says 3 characters but encoder requires exactly 2
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() documents a usually 3-letter shortcut and does not constrain length or charset. DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId rejects any prefix whose length is not exactly 6 (2+2+2) with IllegalArgumentException, and postInit never checks that each grant shortcut is 2 characters or unique against session/token shortcuts. A custom grant that follows the SPI javadoc (or returns null/1/3+ chars) will still be issued an access token, but any later decode of that jti throws and introspection or other endpoints that parse the encoded id fail for those tokens. Duplicate shortcuts are only detected by comparing map sizes after overwrite, so a shortcut collision is a startup failure rather than a clear per-grant error, and a shortcut equal to the reserved "na" unknown marker is silently overwritten.

findings.title: Public Context copy constructor removed and grantType is not refreshed
findings.body: The public OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) copy constructor was deleted in this change, which is a source break for any in-tree or custom grant that cloned a context. grantType is also captured only in the primary constructor via formParams.getFirst(GRANT_TYPE). setFormParams replaces formParams but does not update grantType, so a caller that adjusts the form after construction (a common token-exchange pattern) encodes a stale or null grant. A null grant is then stored as the "na" unknown shortcut, so downstream session/grant optimizations treat the token as an unknown grant.

findings.title: Unused TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory import
findings.body: The new import of TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory is unused; the grant type is set from OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE. Keycloak's unused-import checks will fail the build on this file.
